cells.tense: The work is happening now, and the spark is in it.
cells.ask: let yourself be a beginner again at one piece of what you already do well, and notice that being new here is not a threat to your skill.
cells.sheetLine: You're still discovering something in the work, and it's still teaching you.
cells.core:
The practice has heat in it right now. Not strain, not intensity — a live curiosity that keeps the same exercise fresh on the fiftieth pass. That is what people can't name when they watch: you're still finding something. Skill and openness are running together, and that combination is rarer than you'd guess.

So the question is what this openness is free to feed next. Take the piece you've gotten good at and quietly stopped being curious about. Let yourself be a beginner again at that one piece, and notice that being new here is not a threat to your skill. The practice gets its edge back.
cells.verb: to catch fire before you know what for
cells.place: in the small steady work of getting good at something

cells.tense: You're already living in the version where it's finished and proven.
cells.ask: put the work in front of one person's full attention and let what is actually there be what is there, without polishing it first into something you'd defend.
cells.sheetLine: You're rehearsing the proof instead of doing the practice.
cells.core:
A spark stays alive by being allowed to jump. Done well, this kind of work gets shown at the stage it's actually at, and the showing is part of the making. Yours is being made to carry more than it can hold — you're rehearsing the future it will prove, polishing it before it has earned it, and calling the pressure commitment. That pressure is trying to hurry a thing whose whole value is that it's made slowly.

So bring the work into plain sight before it's ready to be judged. Put it in front of one person's full attention and let what is actually there be what is there, without polishing it first into something you'd defend. Your eye for what's real comes back, and the practice can breathe.

cells.place: in the small steady work of getting good at something

cells.tense: The work carries on, and you're standing just outside the room where it happens.
cells.ask: show one person the effort before it's good, and let closeness to that person do the lighting your own attention can't reach right now.
cells.sheetLine: You're putting in the hours but nobody's on the other end of them.
cells.core:
The practice is meant to be done in the open — not perfectly, just done, with attention. A quiet thing nobody says enough: this kind of work is held by being witnessed, by knowing someone is on the other end of it. That end has gone dark. The hours are still going in, but they're not landing anywhere, and the practice has stopped teaching you.

So stop trying to relight discipline from inside discipline. Show one person the effort before it's good, and let closeness to that person do the lighting your own attention can't reach right now. You get the work back with people in it, not just hours.

cells.tense: You're at the bench every day and you call it just getting through.
cells.ask: name the one thing you're actually moving toward with all this practice, even if the name is clumsy and might change tomorrow.
cells.sheetLine: You've been calling a live practice routine.
cells.core:
By now the fire does show up — the stamina, the small awakenings, a hard exercise starting to feel like home. Done well, this is where the practice becomes yours: the interest underneath the repetition, the thing all these hours are quietly pointing at. A name for it hasn't been said, so the heat reads as habit. The practice is real; the part you're leaving out is the 'for what.'

So say the direction out loud in plain language. Name the one thing you're actually moving toward with all this practice, even if the name is clumsy and might change tomorrow. The heat becomes something you can steer, instead of heat that only keeps the room warm.
